result.reason: The passage is the baraita itself (the Tosefta citation with Rabbi Meir's statement), which the 'Baraita Setup' prose explicitly introduces and describes as the opening text of 12b, whereas the 'Rabbi Meir' section is the essay's commentary/analysis of his position rather than the location of the source text itself.

Both items present Rabbi Yose's ruling and the supporting precedent of Yosef ben Illem, which is exactly what the 'Rabbi Yose' prose section describes, whereas the current placement under 'Eivah & Maalin' discusses the Gemara's explanatory reasoning for why each prohibition applies — content that is not yet present in these two items.

The passage contains both Rabba bar bar Ḥana/Rabbi Yoḥanan's ruling (halakha ke-Rabbi Yose) with the concession about valid service if performed, and Rav Yehuda/Rav's ruling about the first's death — both of which are explicitly discussed together in the 'If He Performs' section's prose, which covers both rulings as a unit.

The passage directly discusses the 'tzara mechayim' concept — the rival-wife-in-lifetime analogy — which is exactly what the 'Met Rishon' prose explains as the Gemara's concern about the second kohen gadol's presence constituting a form of rivalry during the first's lifetime.
The passage discusses exactly the Rabbanan's answer that tumah is common (shchicha) while death is not common, which is precisely what the 'Tumah Shchicha' section's prose describes.

The passage directly discusses Rabbi Yehuda's position that concern for one death is warranted but not two deaths, and the Rabbanan's counter that if any concern exists it applies equally to two deaths — exactly what the 'Two Deaths' section prose describes.

The passage directly addresses the challenge to the Rabbanan about designating a second backup, their response that the kohen gadol is vigilant (zariz), and the explanation that having a rival makes him more vigilant — all of which is precisely what the 'Two Tamei' section prose describes.

The passage specifically discusses whether designation suffices, whether betrothal (kiddushin) suffices, and whether nisuin is required — exactly the content described in the 'Nisu'in Required' prose, ending with the two-houses problem which is merely the closing point of that section before the next heading takes over.
Candidate 3's prose explicitly describes both the 'al menat shetamuti' proposal (item 1) and the 'al menat shelo tamuti' proposal with its fatal flaw (item 2), matching the passage content precisely.
All three items discuss the 'on condition that one of you dies' formulation and Rava's ruling about kerisut, which is precisely what candidate 0's prose describes.

Both items discuss the conditional get scenarios ('on condition that your counterpart does not die' and 'on condition that your counterpart dies') and the midday-overlap problem, which is precisely what the 'Midday Overlap' prose section describes — the current placement is correct.

Both items are part of the Gemara's working-through of the 'both conditional gittin' solution — item 1 raises the objection that both conditions might be fulfilled leaving him with no wife, and item 2 presents the refined solution where one condition depends on the kohen gadol's own entry into the synagogue, exactly matching the 'Both Conditional' prose description.

Both items are the Rav Asi/Rav Avira and Ravina/Rav Sherevya objections about yibbum and arusah respectively, which are explicitly described together in the 'Rav Ashi' section's prose as the two challenges tested against the bayit/nisu'in premises.

Both items — Rava's interpretation of Rabbi Yehuda's 'kol ha'yom' and Abaye's challenge from the baraita about removing a priest mid-service — are explicitly discussed together in the 'Kohen Gadol Exception' prose, which describes exactly this exchange between Rava and Abaye on the meaning of kol ha'yom and the contradiction with Rabbi Yehuda's ruling about maniach avodato v'yotzei.

The passage shows Rava rejecting an initial interpretation and redefining 'kol ha'yom,' which directly matches the prose of candidate 0 describing Rava's revised interpretation of Rabbi Yehuda's position regarding the entire day.
